title: Something Is Taking Round Bites Out of Whales. It's 20 Inches Long

scenes.text: Something is biting perfect circles out of whales.
The wounds are neat craters, about five centimetres across, on dolphins, tuna, even great white sharks.
scenes.keywords: dolphin round wound great white shark

scenes.text: The culprit is the cookiecutter shark, about fifty centimetres long.
Its belly glows green, except for a dark collar that looks like a small fish from below. Bait.
When a predator rises to strike, the shark latches on with its lips, spins, and twists out a plug of flesh.
In 2009 one bit a swimmer off Hawaii. It has even gouged Navy submarines. Nothing is too big to be a cookie.

description:
The cookiecutter shark is only about 50 centimetres long, yet it takes round plugs of flesh out of whales, dolphins, tuna and even great white sharks. Its glowing belly and dark non-glowing collar lure predators close; it latches on with suction lips and spins.
The only documented bite on a living human was a long-distance swimmer off Hawaii in 2009, and the species has bitten the rubber sonar domes of submarines.
Which animal punches furthest above its weight?
subject: cookiecutter shark
first_comment: The cookiecutter sheds its whole lower row of teeth at once and swallows it to recycle the calcium. What is the smallest animal you would not want to meet in the water?
